pmid:31692293.authors: Esteves SC, Santi D, Simoni M
pmid:31692293.title: An update on clinical and surgical interventions to reduce sperm DNA fragmentation in infertile men
pmid:31692293.finding: Best evidence for lowering SDF is varicocele repair; antioxidants and lifestyle change may lower SDF but their effect on pregnancy is unclear.

pmid:24681577.authors: Afeiche MC, Williams PL, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:24681577.title: Meat intake and reproductive parameters among young men.
pmid:24681577.finding: Processed red meat was inversely related to total sperm count (top vs bottom quartile -78 million, P-trend 0.01), driven by lower ejaculate volume; unprocessed red meat, poultry and fish were not related to any semen parameter.

pmid:35565922.authors: Liu YS, Zhang YX, Wang XB, et al.
pmid:35565922.title: Associations between Meat and Vegetable Intake, Cooking Methods, and Asthenozoospermia: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in China.
pmid:35565922.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of unprocessed meat intake had lower odds of asthenozoospermia (OR 0.61) and total meat OR 0.56; processed meat raised the odds (OR 1.44) and stir-frying meat was associated with higher risk (OR 1.58).

pmid:22748101.authors: Agarwal A, Aponte-Mellado A, Premkumar BJ, et al.
pmid:22748101.title: The effects of oxidative stress on female reproduction: a review
pmid:22748101.finding: Narrative review: oxidative stress is implicated in endometriosis, PCOS, unexplained infertility and pregnancy complications; antioxidant evidence is mostly animal/in-vitro and conflicting.

pmid:21220312.authors: Shkolnik K, Tadmor A, Ben-Dor S, et al.
pmid:21220312.title: Reactive oxygen species are indispensable in ovulation
pmid:21220312.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:21220312.finding: In mice, antioxidants injected into the ovarian bursa reduced ovulation and blocked LH-induced cumulus expansion; H2O2 mimicked LH. ROS are an essential pre-ovulatory signal.

pmid:27562289.authors: May-Panloup P, Boucret L, Chao de la Barca JM, et al.
pmid:27562289.title: Ovarian ageing: the role of mitochondria in oocytes and follicles
pmid:27562289.finding: Oocytes are the most mitochondria-rich cells in the body; ageing-related mtDNA instability and impaired mitochondrial biogenesis in oocytes and granulosa cells are closely linked to declining oocyte quality.

pmid:18223651.authors: Cree LM, Samuels DC, de Sousa Lopes SC, et al.
pmid:18223651.title: A reduction of mitochondrial DNA molecules during embryogenesis explains the rapid segregation of genotypes
pmid:18223651.finding: Mouse study: mtDNA is maternally inherited and passes through a genetic bottleneck (partitioning of mtDNA molecules during embryogenesis and germ-cell proliferation) that explains rapid shifts in heteroplasmy between generations.

pmid:24355045.authors: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, et al.
pmid:24355045.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
pmid:24355045.finding: Embryo aneuploidy was lowest at ages 26-30 and rose predictably after 26; the chance of having no euploid embryo was 2-6% at ages 26-37, 33% at 42 and 53% at 44.

pmid:31604276.authors: Gruhn JR, Zielinska AP, Shukla V, et al.
pmid:31604276.title: Chromosome errors in human eggs shape natural fertility over reproductive life span
pmid:31604276.finding: Aneuploidy in human eggs follows a U-curve with age; in older women it is driven by centromeric and more extensive loss of sister-chromatid cohesion.

pmid:32049001.authors: Bertoldo MJ, Listijono DR, Ho WJ, et al.
pmid:32049001.title: NAD(+) Repletion Rescues Female Fertility during Reproductive Aging
pmid:32049001.finding: In aged mice, oocyte NAD+ falls with age; the precursor NMN restored oocyte quality, fertility and embryo development. Mouse data only.

pmid:32755581.authors: Miao Y, Cui Z, Gao Q, et al.
pmid:32755581.title: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Supplementation Reverses the Declining Quality of Maternally Aged Oocytes
pmid:32755581.finding: In naturally aged mice, NMN restored oocyte NAD+, spindle/chromosome structure, fertilization ability and mitochondrial function and lowered ROS. Mouse data only.

pmid:3558758.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results
pmid:3558758.finding: Human follicle growth is very long: the ovulatory follicle comes from a cohort of preantral follicles that differentiated about 85 days earlier; it is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation.

pmid:20362973.title: Human ovarian follicular development: from activation of resting follicles to preovulatory maturation
pmid:20362973.finding: Several months are needed for a growing follicle to reach the preantral stage, then about 70 more days to reach 2 mm before cyclic selection.

pmid:16861701.authors: Das S, Chattopadhyay R, Ghosh S, et al.
pmid:16861701.title: Reactive oxygen species level in follicular fluid--embryo quality marker in IVF?
pmid:16861701.finding: Higher follicular fluid ROS and lipid peroxidation were associated with fertilization failure, pronuclear arrest and poor-grade embryos.

pmid:18339123.authors: Tamura H, Takasaki A, Miwa I, et al.
pmid:18339123.title: Oxidative stress impairs oocyte quality and melatonin protects oocytes from free radical damage and improves fertilization rate
pmid:18339123.finding: Follicular 8-OHdG (oxidative DNA damage) was higher where many oocytes degenerated; melatonin 3 mg/day and/or vitamin E 600 mg/day lowered follicular oxidative markers, and melatonin was associated with better fertilization vs the previous failed cycle (not randomized).

pmid:20643402.authors: Meseguer M, Santiso R, Garrido N, et al.
pmid:20643402.title: Effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on pregnancy outcome depends on oocyte quality
pmid:20643402.finding: Sperm DNA fragmentation lowered pregnancy odds when the woman's own (infertile-patient) oocytes were used, but had no significant effect with donor oocytes, implying good oocytes can compensate for sperm DNA damage.

pmid:20663262.authors: Ménézo Y, Dale B, Cohen M
pmid:20663262.title: DNA damage and repair in human oocytes and embryos: a review
pmid:20663262.finding: Early embryos rely on maternally stored DNA-repair transcripts until embryonic genome activation at the 4-8 cell stage; the oocyte must repair DNA damage brought in by sperm.

pmid:24559617.authors: ACOG Committee on Gynecologic Practice; ASRM Practice Committee
pmid:24559617.title: Female age-related fertility decline. Committee Opinion No. 589
pmid:24559617.finding: ACOG/ASRM: female fecundity declines gradually from about age 32 and more rapidly after 37; evaluate after 6 months of trying at >35 and immediately at >40.

pmid:23303572.authors: Murri M, Luque-Ramírez M, Insenser M, et al.
pmid:23303572.title: Circulating markers of oxidative stress and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:23303572.finding: Women with PCOS had higher circulating malondialdehyde (+47%), homocysteine (+23%) and ADMA, and about 50% lower glutathione, independent of weight excess.

pmid:37580314.authors: Teede HJ, Tay CT, Laven JJE, et al.
pmid:37580314.title: Recommendations From the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
pmid:37580314.finding: 2023 international PCOS guideline (77 evidence-based, 54 consensus recommendations): emphasizes healthy lifestyle and evidence-based medical and fertility therapy; evidence generally low-to-moderate quality.

pmid:28701212.authors: Sanchez AM, Vanni VS, Bartiromo L, et al.
pmid:28701212.title: Is the oocyte quality affected by endometriosis? A review of the literature
pmid:28701212.finding: Systematic review: oocytes from women with endometriosis are more likely to fail in-vitro maturation, show altered morphology and lower mitochondrial content; granulosa cells show more ROS.

pmid:26168799.authors: Hamdan M, Dunselman G, Li TC, et al.
pmid:26168799.title: The impact of endometrioma on IVF/ICSI outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26168799.finding: Endometrioma was associated with fewer oocytes retrieved and more cancelled cycles, but similar live birth rates (OR 0.98); surgery before IVF did not improve outcomes.

pmid:19574447.authors: Wang Q, Ratchford AM, Chi MM, et al.
pmid:19574447.title: Maternal diabetes causes mitochondrial dysfunction and meiotic defects in murine oocytes
pmid:19574447.finding: In diabetic mice, oocytes showed abnormal mitochondrial structure and distribution, lower ATP and TCA metabolites, more spindle defects and higher aneuploidy.

pmid:21170514.authors: Whitworth KW, Baird DD, Stene LC, et al.
pmid:21170514.title: Fecundability among women with type 1 and type 2 diabetes in the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study
pmid:21170514.finding: Fecundability odds were lower in women with type 1 diabetes (FOR 0.76) and type 2 diabetes (FOR 0.64), even with regular cycles.

pmid:19223519.authors: Robker RL, Akison LK, Bennett BD, et al.
pmid:19223519.title: Obese women exhibit differences in ovarian metabolites, hormones, and gene expression compared with moderate-weight women
pmid:19223519.finding: Higher BMI was associated with higher follicular fluid insulin, lactate, triglycerides and C-reactive protein: an altered, more inflammatory follicular environment.

pmid:20861227.authors: Wu LL, Dunning KR, Yang X, et al.
pmid:20861227.title: High-fat diet causes lipotoxicity responses in cumulus-oocyte complexes and decreased fertilization rates
pmid:20861227.finding: High-fat-diet obese mice had lipid-laden oocytes with reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, ER stress, cumulus apoptosis and lower fertilization; ER stress markers were also raised in granulosa cells of obese women.

pmid:30941397.authors: Sermondade N, Huberlant S, Bourhis-Lefebvre V, et al.
pmid:30941397.title: Female obesity is negatively associated with live birth rate following IVF: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:30941397.finding: Obese women (BMI >= 30) had lower live birth rates after IVF than normal-weight women (RR 0.85); worse when combined with PCOS.

pmid:1559293.authors: Kiddy DS, Hamilton-Fairley D, Bush A, et al.
pmid:1559293.title: Improvement in endocrine and ovarian function during dietary treatment of obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:1559293.finding: Women who lost more than 5% of body weight on a 1000 kcal diet had lower insulin, higher SHBG and 9 of 11 improved reproductive function; those losing less than 5% did not improve.

pmid:27192672.authors: Mutsaerts MA, van Oers AM, Groen H, et al.
pmid:27192672.title: Randomized Trial of a Lifestyle Program in Obese Infertile Women
pmid:27192672.finding: LIFEstyle trial: a 6-month lifestyle program before fertility treatment (mean loss 4.4 kg) did not increase healthy term singleton births at 24 months (27.1% vs 35.2%; RR 0.77).

pmid:28854592.authors: Einarsson S, Bergh C, Friberg B, et al.
pmid:28854592.title: Weight reduction intervention for obese infertile women prior to IVF: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:28854592.finding: Intensive weight loss (12 weeks 880 kcal/day, mean -9.4 kg) before IVF did not change IVF live birth (29.6% vs 27.5%), but more spontaneous conceptions occurred (10.5% vs 2.6%).

pmid:28961722.authors: Best D, Avenell A, Bhattacharya S
pmid:28961722.title: How effective are weight-loss interventions for improving fertility in women and men who are overweight or obese? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence
pmid:28961722.finding: In overweight/obese women, reduced-calorie diet and exercise interventions increased pregnancy (RR 1.59) and improved ovulation; miscarriage was not reduced.

pmid:9688387.authors: Augood C, Duckitt K, Templeton AA
pmid:9688387.title: Smoking and female infertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:9688387.finding: Female smokers had higher odds of infertility (OR 1.60) and lower odds of pregnancy per IVF cycle (OR 0.66).

pmid:18927070.authors: Waylen AL, Metwally M, Jones GL, et al.
pmid:18927070.title: Effects of cigarette smoking upon clinical outcomes of assisted reproduction: a meta-analysis
pmid:18927070.finding: Smokers undergoing ART had lower odds of live birth per cycle (OR 0.54) and clinical pregnancy (OR 0.56) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.65).

pmid:30481189.authors: Zhu D, Chung HF, Pandeya N, et al.
pmid:30481189.title: Relationships between intensity, duration, cumulative dose, and timing of smoking with age at menopause: A pooled analysis of individual data from 17 observational studies
pmid:30481189.finding: Current smokers had about twice the risk of premature (RRR 2.05) and early (1.80) menopause, with clear dose-response; women who had quit more than 10 years earlier had the same risk as never smokers.

pmid:18252054.authors: Freour T, Masson D, Mirallie S, et al.
pmid:18252054.title: Active smoking compromises IVF outcome and affects ovarian reserve
pmid:18252054.finding: Active smokers had lower AMH, fewer mature oocytes (8.6 vs 12.1) and lower clinical pregnancy (10% vs 29.6%) than non-smokers.

pmid:38284953.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:38284953.title: Tobacco or marijuana use and infertility: a committee opinion
pmid:38284953.finding: ASRM committee opinion reviewing deleterious effects of tobacco, nicotine and marijuana on conception, ovarian follicular dynamics, gamete mutations and ART outcomes, and smoking-cessation strategies.

pmid:29062133.authors: Fan D, Liu L, Xia Q, et al.
pmid:29062133.title: Female alcohol consumption and fecundability: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29062133.finding: Any alcohol use was associated with lower fecundability (RR 0.87); light (<=12.5 g/day) 0.89, moderate-heavy (>12.5 g/day) 0.77; per 12.5 g/day RR 0.98.

pmid:27581754.authors: Mikkelsen EM, Riis AH, Wise LA, et al.
pmid:27581754.title: Alcohol consumption and fecundability: prospective Danish cohort study
pmid:27581754.finding: Fewer than 14 servings/week had no discernible effect on fecundability; >=14 servings/week FR 0.82 (imprecise).

pmid:21173655.authors: Rossi BV, Berry KF, Hornstein MD, et al.
pmid:21173655.title: Effect of alcohol consumption on in vitro fertilization
pmid:21173655.finding: Women drinking >=4 drinks/week had 16% lower odds of IVF live birth (OR 0.84); 21% lower when both partners did.

pmid:28854726.authors: Abadia L, Chiu YH, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:28854726.title: The association between pre-treatment maternal alcohol and caffeine intake and outcomes of assisted reproduction in a prospectively followed cohort
pmid:28854726.finding: Low-to-moderate pre-treatment alcohol (<=12 g/day) and caffeine (<200 mg/day) were not associated with ART outcomes.

pmid:29276412.authors: Lyngsø J, Ramlau-Hansen CH, Bay B, et al.
pmid:29276412.title: Association between coffee or caffeine consumption and fecundity and fertility: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29276412.finding: Caffeine was associated with spontaneous abortion (RR 1.37 at 300 mg/day; 2.32 at 600 mg/day) but showed little or no association with fecundability or fertility-treatment outcomes.

pmid:27112524.authors: Wesselink AK, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:27112524.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and fecundability in a preconception cohort
pmid:27112524.finding: Female total caffeine intake was not associated with fecundability; male intake >=300 mg/day was (FR 0.72).

pmid:26329421.authors: Chen LW, Wu Y, Neelakantan N, et al.
pmid:26329421.title: Maternal caffeine intake during pregnancy and risk of pregnancy loss: a categorical and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies
pmid:26329421.finding: Caffeine in pregnancy: pregnancy-loss RR 1.02 at 50-149 mg/day, 1.16 at 150-349, 1.40 at 350-699, 1.72 at >=700; +7% per 100 mg/day.

pmid:34815068.authors: ASRM Practice Committee and SREI Practice Committee
pmid:34815068.title: Optimizing natural fertility: a committee opinion
pmid:34815068.finding: ASRM/SREI: >500 mg caffeine/day linked to lower fertility, 1-2 cups/day has no apparent effect; >2 drinks/day best avoided; folic acid >=400 ug/day; insufficient evidence that a specific diet improves natural fertility.

pmid:20228391.authors: Legro RS, Sauer MV, Mottla GL, et al.
pmid:20228391.title: Effect of air quality on assisted human reproduction
pmid:20228391.finding: Higher NO2 at home and at the IVF lab was associated with lower live birth (e.g. OR 0.76 per 0.01 ppm after embryo transfer); PM2.5 during culture was associated with lower conception.

pmid:32951044.authors: La Marca A, Spaggiari G, Domenici D, et al.
pmid:32951044.title: Elevated levels of nitrous dioxide are associated with lower AMH levels: a real-world analysis
pmid:32951044.finding: Higher NO2 (and weakly PM10/PM2.5) exposure was associated with lower AMH; NO2 remained associated after age adjustment.

pmid:31241127.authors: Gaskins AJ, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Fong KC, et al.
pmid:31241127.title: Supplemental Folate and the Relationship Between Traffic-Related Air Pollution and Livebirth Among Women Undergoing Assisted Reproduction
pmid:31241127.finding: Among women taking <800 ug/day supplemental folate, each 20 ppb NO2 was associated with 24% lower odds of live birth; no association at >=800 ug/day.

pmid:26545148.authors: Hauser R, Gaskins AJ, Souter I, et al.
pmid:26545148.title: Urinary Phthalate Metabolite Concentrations and Reproductive Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization: Results from the EARTH Study
pmid:26545148.finding: Highest vs lowest quartile of urinary DEHP metabolites: fewer oocytes and mature oocytes, and 19 percentage points lower clinical pregnancy and live birth per cycle.

pmid:20002217.authors: Mok-Lin E, Ehrlich S, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:20002217.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and ovarian response among women undergoing IVF
pmid:20002217.finding: Each log-unit increase in urinary BPA was associated with 12% fewer oocytes retrieved and lower peak estradiol.

pmid:34337160.authors: Butts CD, Bloom MS, McGough A, et al.
pmid:34337160.title: Toxic elements in follicular fluid adversely influence the likelihood of pregnancy and live birth in women undergoing IVF
pmid:34337160.finding: Follicular fluid mercury above ~0.51 ug/L and higher lead were associated with lower live birth after IVF (Pb RR 0.68).

pmid:12525451.authors: Wallace WH, Thomson AB, Kelsey TW
pmid:12525451.title: The radiosensitivity of the human oocyte
pmid:12525451.finding: Modelling estimates the radiation dose that destroys half of human oocytes (LD50) at less than 2 Gy.

pmid:29620997.authors: Oktay K, Harvey BE, Partridge AH, et al.
pmid:29620997.title: Fertility Preservation in Patients With Cancer: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update
pmid:29620997.finding: ASCO: discuss infertility risk before cancer treatment as early as possible; oocyte and embryo cryopreservation are standard; GnRH agonists are not a substitute for proven preservation methods.

pmid:37752011.authors: Mountjoy M, Ackerman KE, Bailey DM, et al.
pmid:37752011.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee's (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs)
pmid:37752011.finding: IOC 2023 consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport: low energy availability causes health effects including reproductive dysfunction, with a clinical assessment tool for diagnosis.

pmid:19801570.authors: Gudmundsdottir SL, Flanders WD, Augestad LB
pmid:19801570.title: Physical activity and fertility in women: the North-Trøndelag Health Study
pmid:19801570.finding: Women active on most days had 3.2-fold odds of fertility problems and exercising to exhaustion 2.3-fold, vs low activity; no association at lower activity levels.

pmid:22425198.authors: Wise LA, Rothman KJ, Mikkelsen EM, et al.
pmid:22425198.title: A prospective cohort study of physical activity and time to pregnancy
pmid:22425198.finding: Vigorous activity >=5 h/week vs none: fecundability ratio 0.68 (lean women); moderate activity >=5 h/week: 1.18; no harm from vigorous activity in women with BMI >=25.

pmid:27474489.authors: Gaskins AJ, Williams PL, Keller MG, et al.
pmid:27474489.title: Maternal physical and sedentary activities in relation to reproductive outcomes following IVF
pmid:27474489.finding: Pre-treatment moderate-to-vigorous activity (median 2.8 h/week) was not associated with IVF outcomes; some vigorous activities were associated with higher live birth.

pmid:31304974.authors: Mena GP, Mielke GI, Brown WJ
pmid:31304974.title: The effect of physical activity on reproductive health outcomes in young women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:31304974.finding: Physical-activity interventions increased pregnancy (RR 2.10) and live birth (RR 2.11) vs no therapy in women with reproductive problems (small number of trials).

pmid:24901274.authors: Stocker LJ, Macklon NS, Cheong YC, et al.
pmid:24901274.title: Influence of shift work on early reproductive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:24901274.finding: Shift work was associated with menstrual disruption (aOR 1.15); infertility association was not robust after adjustment (aOR 1.11); night shifts were associated with early pregnancy loss (aOR 1.41).

pmid:30987736.authors: Willis SK, Hatch EE, Wesselink AK, et al.
pmid:30987736.title: Female sleep patterns, shift work, and fecundability in a North American preconception cohort study
pmid:30987736.finding: Trouble sleeping >50% of the time was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.87); <6 h sleep FR 0.89 (imprecise); shift work was not associated.

pmid:24664130.authors: Lynch CD, Sundaram R, Maisog JM, et al.
pmid:24664130.title: Preconception stress increases the risk of infertility: results from a couple-based prospective cohort study--the LIFE study
pmid:24664130.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of salivary alpha-amylase (stress marker) was associated with 29% lower fecundability and 2-fold infertility risk; cortisol was not associated.

pmid:21345903.authors: Boivin J, Griffiths E, Venetis CA
pmid:21345903.title: Emotional distress in infertile women and failure of assisted reproductive technologies: meta-analysis of prospective psychosocial studies
pmid:21345903.finding: Pre-treatment anxiety or depression was not associated with pregnancy after a cycle of ART.

pmid:29390148.authors: Karayiannis D, Kontogianni MD, Mendorou C, et al.
pmid:29390148.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and IVF success rate among non-obese women attempting fertility
pmid:29390148.finding: Lowest vs highest tertile of Mediterranean diet score had lower live birth (26.6% vs 48.8%; adjusted RR 0.32); association seen only in women under 35; no effect on oocyte or embryo measures.

pmid:30742825.authors: Gaskins AJ, Nassan FL, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:30742825.title: Dietary patterns and outcomes of assisted reproduction
pmid:30742825.finding: The profertility diet was associated with 53% higher odds of live birth per SD; top vs bottom quartile +28 percentage points; not related to oocyte counts. Mediterranean diet benefit plateaued after the second quartile.

pmid:20189169.authors: Vujkovic M, de Vries JH, Lindemans J, et al.
pmid:20189169.title: The preconception Mediterranean dietary pattern in couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection treatment increases the chance of pregnancy
pmid:20189169.finding: High couple adherence to a Mediterranean dietary pattern was associated with higher pregnancy odds after IVF/ICSI (OR 1.4) and higher folate and vitamin B6 in blood and follicular fluid.

pmid:36346903.authors: Muffone ARMC, de Oliveira Lübke PDP, Rabito EI
pmid:36346903.title: Mediterranean diet and infertility: a systematic review with meta-analysis of cohort studies
pmid:36346903.finding: Pooled evidence linking Mediterranean diet adherence to live birth and pregnancy was inconsistent and insufficient to support clinical application.

pmid:28844822.title: Diet and fertility: a review
pmid:28844822.finding: Review: supplemental folic acid (above neural-tube-defect doses) is consistently associated with better fertility; antioxidant supplements do not help women in fertility treatment; omega-3s appear beneficial; vitamin D matters mainly in deficiency.

pmid:17978119.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17978119.title: Diet and lifestyle in the prevention of ovulatory disorder infertility
pmid:17978119.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of a 'fertility diet' score was associated with 66% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.34); five or more low-risk lifestyle factors with 69% lower risk.

pmid:25198264.authors: Gaskins AJ, Afeiche MC, Wright DL, et al.
pmid:25198264.title: Dietary folate and reproductive success among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:25198264.finding: Supplemental folate >800 ug/day vs <400 ug/day was associated with a 20 percentage-point higher live birth rate after ART.

pmid:26081493.authors: Cueto HT, Riis AH, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:26081493.title: Folic acid supplementation and fecundability: a Danish prospective cohort study
pmid:26081493.finding: Folic acid or multivitamin supplementation was associated with higher fecundability (FR 1.15), more so with irregular cycles.

pmid:37526713.title: Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects: US Preventive Services Task Force Reaffirmation Recommendation Statement
pmid:37526713.finding: USPSTF: everyone planning or capable of pregnancy should take a daily supplement containing 0.4-0.8 mg (400-800 ug) folic acid (A recommendation).

pmid:29149263.authors: Chu J, Gallos I, Tobias A, et al.
pmid:29149263.title: Vitamin D and assisted reproductive treatment outcome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:29149263.finding: Vitamin D-replete women undergoing ART had higher live birth than deficient/insufficient women (OR 1.33); no association with miscarriage.

pmid:35370977.authors: Zhou X, Wu X, Luo X, et al.
pmid:35370977.title: Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation on In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis of 5 Randomized Controlled Trials
pmid:35370977.finding: In vitamin D-deficient infertile women, supplementation raised chemical pregnancy (RR 1.53) but not clinical pregnancy (RR 1.34, NS) or embryo quality.

pmid:29136189.authors: Chiu YH, Karmon AE, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:29136189.title: Serum omega-3 fatty acids and treatment outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:29136189.finding: Each 1% higher serum long-chain omega-3 was associated with 8% higher probability of live birth after ART.

pmid:22978268.authors: Nehra D, Le HD, Fallon EM, et al.
pmid:22978268.title: Prolonging the female reproductive lifespan and improving egg quality with dietary omega-3 fatty acids
pmid:22978268.finding: In mice, omega-3-rich diets prolonged reproductive function and improved oocyte quality at advanced maternal age; omega-6-rich diets worsened it.

pmid:32851663.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:32851663.title: Antioxidants for female subfertility
pmid:32851663.finding: Very low-quality evidence: antioxidants might raise live birth (OR 1.81) but evidence is unreliable; 2026 editorial note: 7 included trials since retracted and 2 under expression of concern (conclusions retained).

pmid:29587861.authors: Xu Y, Nisenblat V, Lu C, et al.
pmid:29587861.title: Pretreatment with coenzyme Q10 improves ovarian response and embryo quality in low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:29587861.n: 186 women <35 with poor ovarian reserve (169 analysed)
pmid:29587861.finding: CoQ10 600 mg/day (200 mg three times daily) for 60 days before IVF increased oocytes retrieved (median 4 vs 2), fertilization and good embryos; live birth 29% vs 16% was not statistically significant.

pmid:26111777.authors: Ben-Meir A, Burstein E, Borrego-Alvarez A, et al.
pmid:26111777.title: Coenzyme Q10 restores oocyte mitochondrial function and fertility during reproductive aging
pmid:26111777.finding: Oocyte ageing in mice and humans involves reduced CoQ-synthesis enzymes and lower ATP; CoQ10 reversed age-related oocyte deficits in mice.

pmid:32767206.authors: Florou P, Anagnostis P, Theocharis P, et al.
pmid:32767206.title: Does coenzyme Q(10) supplementation improve fertility outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology procedures? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
pmid:32767206.finding: CoQ10 increased clinical pregnancy (28.8% vs 14.1%; OR 2.44) but not live birth (OR 1.67, NS) or miscarriage.

pmid:32045470.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang C, Shu J, et al.
pmid:32045470.title: Adjuvant treatment strategies in ovarian stimulation for poor responders undergoing IVF: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmid:32045470.finding: In poor responders, DHEA (OR 2.46) and CoQ10 (OR 2.22) were associated with higher clinical pregnancy vs control; CoQ10 had the lowest cancellation rate.

pmid:32292388.authors: Hu KL, Ye X, Wang S, et al.
pmid:32292388.title: Melatonin Application in Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
pmid:32292388.finding: Melatonin increased clinical pregnancy (OR 1.43) and oocyte/embryo counts but not live birth (OR 1.38, 3 RCTs, NS); low-quality evidence.

pmid:31583699.authors: Fernando S, Wallace EM, Rombauts L, et al.
pmid:31583699.title: The effect of melatonin on ultrasound markers of follicular development: A double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial
pmid:31583699.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:31583699.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily during IVF stimulation did not change follicle number or ovarian vascular indices vs placebo (pilot).

pmid:30570133.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:30570133.title: Inositol for subfertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30570133.finding: Very low-quality evidence; uncertain whether myo-inositol improves live birth (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.75-7.83) or clinical pregnancy in PCOS before IVF.

pmid:38163998.authors: Fitz V, Graca S, Mahalingaiah S, et al.
pmid:38163998.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines
pmid:38163998.finding: For the 2023 PCOS guideline: inositol evidence is limited and inconclusive; possible metabolic benefits; little difference from metformin for reproductive outcomes.

pmid:26507336.authors: Pacchiarotti A, Carlomagno G, Antonini G, et al.
pmid:26507336.title: Effect of myo-inositol and melatonin versus myo-inositol, in a randomized controlled trial, for improving in vitro fertilization of patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome
pmid:26507336.finding: RETRACTED (2026). Claimed myo-inositol 4 g + folic acid 400 ug + melatonin 3 mg improved oocyte and embryo quality; should not be relied on.

pmid:25653680.authors: Thakker D, Raval A, Patel I, et al.
pmid:25653680.title: N-acetylcysteine for polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials
pmid:25653680.finding: NAC improved ovulation and pregnancy vs placebo but was inferior to metformin; trials had high risk of bias.

pmid:15705376.authors: Rizk AY, Bedaiwy MA, Al-Inany HG
pmid:15705376.title: N-acetyl-cysteine is a novel adjuvant to clomiphene citrate in clomiphene citrate-resistant patients with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:15705376.finding: NAC 1.2 g/day added to clomiphene raised ovulation (49.3% vs 1.3%) and pregnancy (21.3% vs 0%) vs placebo.

pmid:38837771.authors: Naik S, Lepine S, Nagels HE, et al.
pmid:38837771.title: Androgens (dehydroepiandrosterone or testosterone) for women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:38837771.finding: Cochrane: DHEA probably makes little or no difference to live birth in poor responders (OR 1.30, NS, moderate certainty); testosterone probably improves it (OR 2.53).

pmid:20729538.authors: Wiser A, Gonen O, Ghetler Y, et al.
pmid:20729538.title: Addition of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) for poor-responder patients before and during IVF treatment improves the pregnancy rate: a randomized prospective study
pmid:20729538.finding: DHEA 75 mg/day before and during IVF was associated with higher live birth (23.1% vs 4.0%) in a very small trial.

pmid:25015747.authors: Ismail AM, Hamed AH, Saso S, et al.
pmid:25015747.title: Adding L-carnitine to clomiphene resistant PCOS women improves the quality of ovulation and the pregnancy rate. A randomized clinical trial
pmid:25015747.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:25015747.finding: RETRACTED. Claimed L-carnitine 3 g/day with clomiphene raised pregnancy from 5.8% to 51.5%; should not be relied on.

pmid:32273814.title: Preconception resveratrol intake against infertility: Friend or foe?
pmid:32273814.finding: Resveratrol may support ovarian function via SIRT1 but suppresses endometrial decidualization (anti-deciduogenic) and its teratogenicity is unknown; avoid in the luteal phase and pregnancy.

pmid:31160243.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K, Ikemoto Y, et al.
pmid:31160243.title: Influence of resveratrol supplementation on IVF-embryo transfer cycle outcomes
pmid:31160243.finding: Resveratrol 200 mg/day during embryo-transfer cycles was associated with lower clinical pregnancy (OR 0.54) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.60).

pmid:38987824.authors: Ardehjani NA, Agha-Hosseini M, Nashtaei MS, et al.
pmid:38987824.title: Resveratrol ameliorates mitochondrial biogenesis and reproductive outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing assisted reproduction: a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmid:38987824.finding: Resveratrol 800 mg/day for 60 days lowered follicular fluid oxidative stress and raised oocyte maturity and good-quality embryos, but pregnancy rates did not differ.

pmid:33345661.authors: Di Tucci C, Galati G, Mattei G, et al.
pmid:33345661.title: The role of alpha lipoic acid in female and male infertility: a systematic review
pmid:33345661.finding: Systematic review (28 articles): alpha-lipoic acid shows some positive effects on oocyte maturation, embryo grade and endometriosis pain, but clinical evidence is limited and more trials are needed.

pmid:37747409.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, et al.
pmid:37747409.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine†
pmid:37747409.finding: ESHRE add-ons recommendations: antioxidant therapy lacks reliable evidence of higher live birth and is not recommended in ART; routine adjuncts (GH, DHEA, testosterone, metformin) are not supported.

pmid:32395637.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation; Bosch E, Broer S, et al.
pmid:32395637.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI(†)
pmid:32395637.finding: ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline: hormone pre-treatment and adjuvants (metformin, growth hormone, testosterone, DHEA, aspirin, sildenafil) are not recommended for improving efficacy.

pmid:20685716.authors: Dechanet C, Anahory T, Mathieu Daude JC, et al.
pmid:20685716.title: Effects of cigarette smoking on reproduction
pmid:20685716.finding: Systematic review: cigarette smoke contains thousands of toxicants (nicotine, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, cadmium) that target folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis and every other reproductive stage, dose-dependently.

pmid:25788567.authors: Hahn KA, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:25788567.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and risk of spontaneous abortion
pmid:25788567.finding: Preconception caffeine was not associated with miscarriage (HR 1.09 for >=300 vs <100 mg/day), whereas early-pregnancy intake of 100-299 mg/day was (HR ~1.5-1.6).

pmid:30921477.authors: Lim SS, Hutchison SK, Van Ryswyk E, et al.
pmid:30921477.title: Lifestyle changes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30921477.finding: Cochrane: lifestyle interventions in PCOS may modestly reduce weight and free androgen index; no trial reported live birth or miscarriage.

pmid:32514568.authors: Szymanska KJ, Tan X, Oktay K
pmid:32514568.title: Unraveling the mechanisms of chemotherapy-induced damage to human primordial follicle reserve: road to developing therapeutics for fertility preservation and reversing ovarian aging
pmid:32514568.finding: Gonadotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) induces DNA double-strand breaks and apoptosis of primordial-follicle oocytes within 12-24 h, plus stromal and microvascular damage.

pmid:30895239.authors: Fernando S, Biggs SN, Horne RSC, et al.
pmid:30895239.title: The impact of melatonin on the sleep patterns of women undergoing IVF: a double blind RCT
pmid:30895239.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily from cycle day 2 to egg retrieval did not cause daytime sleepiness or change objective sleep vs placebo.

options.label: Egg quality
options.note: Trying to conceive or pregnant: keep caffeine under about 200 mg/day (roughly 2 cups of coffee), mainly because of miscarriage risk. Take folic acid (400–800 µg/day) starting at least a month before conception.

options.label: Yes, tobacco
options.note: Quitting is the single largest lever on this site. In studies, F2-isoprostanes fell within 2–4 weeks of quitting; semen quality improves over about 3 months. Cutting down without quitting did not lower oxidative markers in an RCT. Avoid beta-carotene supplements while you smoke: they raised lung cancer risk in smokers.

questions.label: Body mass index (BMI)?
questions.help: Rough is fine. BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)².

options.label: Under 18.5
options.note: Being underweight or under-fuelled (low energy availability) can disrupt ovulation and hormone levels. Calorie restriction isn't for you.

questions.label: How would you describe your diet?

options.label: Lots of fast or processed food
Heavy traffic or wildfire smoke nearby
Wood stove, or gas cooking without a hood

questions.label: Are you taking any of these?

options.label: High-dose vitamin C/E or an 'antioxidant formula'
Sauna, hot tub, or hot baths weekly
Laptop on lap, tight underwear, hot job, or long sitting

questions.label: Using testosterone, anabolic steroids, or SARMs?

options.label: Yes
options.note: Exogenous testosterone shuts down sperm production. Come off it only with a doctor (often a urologist or reproductive endocrinologist); recovery can take many months to over a year.

questions.label: Has a doctor found a varicocele?

options.label: Never been examined
options.note: A urologist can check for a varicocele with a quick physical exam. Clinical varicocele is the most common correctable cause of high sperm DNA fragmentation.

questions.label: Fever or flu-like illness in the past 3 months?

options.label: Yes
options.note: Semen quality and DNA integrity can dip for 2–3 months after a fever. If you're getting a semen analysis or DNA fragmentation test, time it accordingly.

questions.label: Any results or treatment so far?

options.label: White cells in semen or a genital infection

questions.label: Age of the person whose eggs are being used?

options.note: Age is the dominant factor in egg quality, mostly through chromosome errors, and no supplement or lifestyle change has been shown to reverse it. Time matters more than any item below; if you're not pregnant after 6 months of trying, see a fertility specialist.

options.label: 40 or older
options.note: Age is the dominant factor in egg quality, mostly through chromosome errors, and nothing has been shown to reverse it in humans. See a fertility specialist promptly; the items below support the odds but won't offset age.

options.label: IVF, told I'm a poor responder
options.note: For poor responders, CoQ10 (600 mg/day for about 60 days before stimulation) has the best trial support among supplements: more eggs and better embryos, but no significant difference in live birth yet. Discuss with your clinic.

guide.footer: This plan is a starting point built from impact ratings and your answers, not a prescription. Effects on sperm show up after about 2–3 months (one spermatogenic cycle) and on eggs after about 3 months (folliculogenesis), so start early. Check any supplement with a clinician, especially when trying to conceive.
